prompt:
Add a `heading_offset` option to `markdown.Markdown` (and `markdown.markdown`): a whole number from 0 to 5, default 0, that shifts the level of every heading Markdown produces by that many (an `h1` becomes an `h2` with 1), never beyond `h6`. Any other value raises `ValueError`.
- It applies to hash and underline headings, and to headings from extensions such as `md_in_html`.
- The `toc` extension sees the shifted levels (its tokens and `toc_depth`).
- The command line gets `--heading-offset N`.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: Added a `heading_offset` option (0–5, default 0) to `Markdown` and `markdown.markdown`. Any other value, including `True`, `1.0` and `'1'`, raises `ValueError`. A new tree processor shifts headings, never past `h6`. It runs before every other tree processor, so `toc` tokens and `toc_depth` see the shifted levels, and it also shifts headings from `md_in_html`; a toc `baselevel` adds on top of the offset. Raw HTML headings (e.g. a plain `<h1>`) stay as they are. The CLI has `--heading-offset N` and rejects values outside 0–5 with an error message. Docs and changelog are updated with new tests, and the full suite passes (112 skipped). Not done: flake8 isn't installed, so lint wasn't run, and headings `md_in_html` leaves in its stash for the final output stage are covered by the code but have no test.
